daisy.also: Oxeye daisy (Leucanthemum vulgare) and other white-rayed daisies
daisy.description: A ring of white ray florets around a yellow disc. What looks like one flower is really a head of hundreds of tiny florets. Common in lawns, meadows and roadsides across temperate regions.
look_for: White petals (ray florets) around a flat yellow centre
Leaves in a rosette at the base
Flower heads close at night and in dull weather

dandelion.description: A bright yellow head made only of strap-shaped florets, followed by the familiar round seed head ('clock'). The stems are hollow and leak a milky sap when broken.
look_for: All-yellow head with no separate centre
Deeply toothed leaves in a basal rosette
Leafless hollow stem with milky sap

rose.also: Garden roses and wild roses such as dog rose (Rosa canina)
rose.description: Woody shrubs and climbers with prickly stems and compound leaves. Garden roses usually have many layered petals; wild roses have five petals and a ring of stamens.
look_for: Red or orange hips after flowering

sunflower.description: A tall annual with a single large head: yellow ray florets around a wide brown or purple disc whose florets spiral outward in Fibonacci patterns. Young heads follow the sun across the sky.
look_for: Very large head, often wider than a hand
Dark central disc much wider than in a daisy
Rough, hairy stem and broad heart-shaped leaves

tulip.also: Garden tulip cultivars (Tulipa gesneriana) and wild tulips
tulip.description: Spring bulbs with a cup-shaped flower of six tepals on a single upright stem. Garden cultivars come in nearly every colour except true blue.
look_for: Cup or goblet-shaped flower with six tepals
Two to four broad, bluish-green leaves at the base
